skill.name: ux-waiting-audit
skill.description: Audit UX waiting states for web applications with long-running operations (30+ seconds). Use when asked to evaluate, audit, or analyze a product's loading states, wait times, progress indicators, or user experience during slow operations. Requires browser automation (Chrome MCP tools). Generates comprehensive reports with screenshots, checklist evaluation, and prioritized recommendations.
skill.summary: Evaluate long-running web operations through timed screenshots, waiting-state checks, and prioritized UX recommendations.
skill.author: BayramAnnakov

security_audit.summary: All 34 static findings are false positives caused by example URLs, a standard installation path, Markdown formatting, and screenshot comments without upload behavior. Semantic review found real privacy and interaction risks in requesting login credentials, capturing authenticated screens without redaction guidance, and submitting forms without explicit confirmation.

remediation.issue: The workflow asks users for login credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Require temporary test accounts and let users enter secrets directly. Never request, store, repeat, or include credentials in reports.

remediation.issue: Screenshots and reports may contain sensitive authenticated content.
remediation.suggestion: Obtain consent, define capture scope, redact sensitive fields, minimize retention, and exclude confidential content from generated reports.

remediation.issue: Direct form submission and coordinate clicks can trigger unintended actions.
remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation before submissions or consequential clicks. Prefer disposable test data and avoid destructive production workflows.

content.user_title: Audit Long-Running Web App Waiting States
content.value_statement: Long-running web operations can feel stalled and cause users to abandon important tasks. This skill captures timed states, evaluates waiting feedback, and produces prioritized improvements.
actual_capabilities: Navigates to a supplied web application using compatible browser automation tools.
Captures screenshots at operation start, timed intervals, and completion.
Inspects visible text and DOM signals for spinners, progress bars, counters, and partial results.
Evaluates progressive value, heartbeat indicators, time estimates, interruption options, and anxiety reduction.
Compares waiting states across a timestamped timeline.
Produces a Markdown audit with strengths, gaps, quick wins, and prioritized recommendations.
limitations: Requires compatible browser automation and permission to access the target application.
Depends on user guidance when navigation, authentication, or operation triggers are unclear.
Cannot guarantee reliable timing or error simulation in production environments.
Referenced checklist, report template, and capture helper files are absent from this package.

use_cases.title: Review AI Task Feedback
use_cases.description: Assess whether research, generation, or analysis workflows communicate progress during waits longer than 30 seconds.

use_cases.title: Validate Release Readiness
use_cases.description: Capture a repeatable waiting-state timeline before shipping a slow report, export, or deployment workflow.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Loading Improvements
use_cases.description: Convert observed waiting problems into clear priorities for progress, cancellation, partial results, and completion feedback.

prompt_templates.title: Audit One Waiting State
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the waiting experience at [URL] for [operation]. Ask before interacting, capture start and completion, then list the three highest-impact improvements.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one accessible operation

prompt_templates.title: Capture a Timed Timeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [operation] at [URL]. After I trigger it, capture states at start, 10 seconds, 30 seconds, and completion. Compare visible feedback.
prompt_templates.scenario: User manually triggers an authenticated operation

prompt_templates.title: Score a Complete Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [operation] in the approved test environment. Evaluate progress, time estimates, partial value, cancellation, errors, and completion. Produce prioritized recommendations.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Normal and Failure States
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [operation] in staging under normal, slow, interrupted, and timeout conditions. Confirm each consequential action. Compare timelines and propose measurable acceptance criteria.

output_examples.input: Audit a 45-second report generation workflow after I start it.
output: Strength: The interface shows a clear active status and preserves navigation.
Critical gap: Users receive no progress estimate or partial results.
Priority: Add stage labels, cancellation, and a completion notification.

output_examples.input: Compare the loading experience at start, 10 seconds, 30 seconds, and completion.
output: Start: A spinner appears, but the operation is not named.
10 seconds: No visible change confirms continued activity.
30 seconds: The interface still lacks progress or time guidance.
Completion: Results appear without a distinct completion signal.

best_practices: Use a staging environment, temporary account, and disposable test data.
Confirm the operation, expected duration, capture scope, and sensitive areas before starting.
Redact screenshots and connect every recommendation to timestamped visual evidence.
anti_patterns: Do not request passwords, tokens, production credentials, or unrelated customer data.
Do not submit forms, click destructive controls, or simulate failures without explicit confirmation.
Do not treat a spinner alone as sufficient evidence of a usable waiting experience.

faq.question: What applications can this skill audit?
faq.answer: It can audit browser-accessible web applications with operations lasting about 30 seconds or longer.

faq.question: Does the skill need login credentials?
faq.answer: No. Use a temporary test account and enter credentials yourself through the approved browser session.

faq.question: What does the audit capture?
faq.answer: It captures approved screenshots and visible state signals at operation start, timed intervals, and completion.

faq.question: Can it test production workflows?
faq.answer: A staging environment is preferred. Production testing requires explicit authorization, limited scope, and non-destructive actions.

faq.question: What report does it produce?
faq.answer: It produces a Markdown report with timeline observations, strengths, critical gaps, quick wins, and prioritized recommendations.

faq.question: Are all referenced support files included?
faq.answer: No. The audited package contains only README.md and SKILL.md, while the instructions reference additional files.
